Aisha — thanks for the details. Short answers up front, then specifics below.

Recommendation summary:
- Launch: US-East dedicated pool (NVIDIA H100 equivalent), 8 nodes (32 GPUs) baseline to support sustained 120 TPS with headroom.
- Autoscale: target floor 8 nodes, ceiling 24 nodes (96 GPUs) with scale-up aggressiveness tuned to sustained 5-minute averages to avoid thrash.
- Burst policy: enable short spike capacity using pre-warmed warm-standby nodes (allow 10-15 minute spikes up to 250 TPS), and fall back to auto-scale when spike lasts >15 minutes.
- EU support: recommend a follow-on EU-West pool (regional separate) for GDPR. We can enable cross-region routing after launch if needed.

Details / rationale:
- Model: image-gen + search model combo has moderate KV cache needs; we recommend GPU type with 80GB memory for stable serving and room for quantized variants.
- Warm pool: we propose a 20% warm buffer (6 GPUs) spun in a light-weight preloaded image to absorb immediate spikes. That reduces cold-start latencies during bursts.
- Autoscale thresholds: scale-up at 80% CPU/GPU utilization sustained over 5 min, scale-down after utilization <50% for 10 min. Token-based batching will reduce per-token cost; we'll enable continuous batching with a max latency budget of 50ms for batch aggregation.
- Cost estimate: baseline monthly compute range in the workbook; expect +/- 20% variation depending on sustained batch sizes. See attached estimate for line items.

Attachments: acme_capacity_estimate.xlsx

If that aligns, we'll prepare a provisioning runbook and an ops playbook for incident response and burst gating. I can draft those once we lock regions and the MLP.

Thanks,
